name: South Korea

facts.religion: No religion about 50%, Protestant about 20%, Buddhist about 16%, Catholic about 11%

snapshot: Courts sentenced former president Yoon Suk Yeol to life for his 2024 martial law attempt, then added 30 years for a plot to provoke North Korea.
culture: The Korean Wave, from BTS and Blackpink to "Squid Game" and Oscar-winning "Parasite", has made South Korean culture a global force. Hangul, the alphabet invented in the 15th century, is celebrated with a national holiday. Chuseok and Lunar New Year bring family gatherings, and kimchi-making is a shared tradition.
society: South Korea went from war-ravaged poverty to one of the world's richest economies, with Samsung, Hyundai and SK Hynix as global giants. It has the world's lowest birth rate, under 0.8 children per woman, and intense competition in schools and jobs. Its democracy, won through mass protest in 1987, survived the 2024 martial law crisis.
situation: South Korea was a military dictatorship until 1987, and its democracy was built by people who were jailed and beaten for it. That history is why Yoon Suk Yeol's attempt to impose martial law on the night of 3 December 2024, sending troops to parliament, was met with crowds blocking soldiers and lawmakers climbing over fences to vote it down within hours. In 2026, the courts finished what the crowds started.

On 19 February, a Seoul court sentenced Yoon to life in prison for leading an insurrection, the first elected leader of the democratic era to receive the maximum custodial sentence; prosecutors had sought the death penalty (TIME via AOL). His former prime minister got 23 years. In June another court gave Yoon 30 more years for conspiring to send military drones over Pyongyang in October 2024 to manufacture a pretext for martial law, convicting him of aiding the enemy (Reuters via Daily Mirror). He joins a long line of former presidents who have gone to prison, but even so has become a figurehead for South Korea's populist right. President Lee Jae-myung, whom Yoon had planned to arrest that night, has governed since June 2025, and his Democratic Party won most of the races in June's local elections.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for a single five-year term and heads the government; the 300-seat National Assembly can impeach the president, as it did Yoon, subject to the Constitutional Court.
holders: President Lee Jae-myung (Democratic Party), in office since June 2025.

conflicts.name: Korean peninsula (North Korean missile tests and Russia alliance)
